forces.title: Sustained infrastructure investment driving MCE demand
forces.description: India's infrastructure build-out across roads, railways, ports, airports, and urban/logistics systems is creating deep and widening demand for Mining and Construction Equipment (MCE). This includes earthmoving, concrete, lifting, tunnelling, and material-handling equipment, fueled by government allocations like INR 2.9 lakh crore for Road Transport and Highways and INR 2.5 lakh crore for railways in 2025. This sustained capital expenditure ensures long-term growth for MCE manufacturers.
forces.source_title: Pressing the Throttle: Unlocking India’s Mining and Construction Equipment Industry’s Potential

forces.title: Mining growth and mineral security fueling advanced equipment demand
forces.description: A sharper focus on mineral security and mining growth, supported by MMDR Act amendments, is driving demand for advanced equipment across coal, metals, and critical minerals. Iron ore, limestone, and coal production have significantly increased, with new frontiers in drilling, excavation, hauling, and underground systems. This is ultimately driven by rising downstream consumption in industries like steel and cement, ensuring a continuous pull for mineral extraction and processing equipment.
forces.source_title: Pressing the Throttle: Unlocking India’s Mining and Construction Equipment Industry’s Potential

forces.title: Deeper localization by OEMs strengthens manufacturing and cost competitiveness
forces.description: Global and domestic OEMs are increasing their local production and engineering footprint in India, with localization levels rising to around 50%. This deepens the manufacturing base and improves cost economics for Indian players, making them more competitive domestically and in export markets. The establishment of engineering, R&D, and capability centers for global platforms, exemplified by Sandvik and BEML, further shifts India from import dependence to export competitiveness.
forces.source_title: Pressing the Throttle: Unlocking India’s Mining and Construction Equipment Industry’s Potential

forces.title: Low mechanisation intensity provides substantial growth headroom
forces.description: India's mechanisation intensity in mining and construction is significantly below global benchmarks, at roughly half the worldwide level. This gap represents a substantial runway for growth for the Capital Goods & Machinery sector. As infrastructure and mining demand remain structurally strong and mechanisation deepens across the country, the adoption of machinery will increase, driving higher volumes and value for equipment manufacturers.
forces.source_title: Pressing the Throttle: Unlocking India’s Mining and Construction Equipment Industry’s Potential

forces.title: Government capital expenditure boosts demand for Capital Goods
forces.description: The Indian government's Union Budget FY27 announced a significant capital expenditure of Rs. 15.48 lakh crore (US$ 172.00 billion), with states also budgeting a 15% rise in capital outlay for FY27. This strong investment focus across infrastructure, manufacturing, and urban development, coupled with initiatives like the Urban Infrastructure Development Fund, directly drives demand for Capital Goods & Machinery, ensuring a robust order pipeline for the sector.

forces.title: Liberal policy regime supports growth in Capital Goods sector
forces.description: India's capital goods sector benefits from a liberal policy regime, featuring no industrial licensing, 100% FDI under the automatic route (except from land-border nations), unrestricted technology transfer payments, and no import or export restrictions. The National Capital Goods Policy (2016) further aims to significantly boost the sector's manufacturing share, double production, and increase exports, creating a highly conducive environment for investment and expansion.
forces.source_title: Engineering And Capital Goods Industry In India

forces.title: Shift to cleaner powertrains remaking MCE industry
forces.description: The Mining and Construction Equipment (MCE) industry is undergoing a structural shift towards cleaner powertrains, including cleaner diesel (CEV Stage V norms), battery-electric vehicles (BEVs) for underground mining, and hydrogen (prototype stage for heavy haul trucks). This transition is driven by sustainability requirements, stringent emissions regulations, and operational benefits, requiring MCE OEMs to build battery-electric capabilities and navigate the economic factors for adoption, such as charging infrastructure.
forces.source_title: Pressing the Throttle: Unlocking India’s Mining and Construction Equipment Industry’s Potential

forces.title: Digitalization and AI transforming MCE into intelligent systems
forces.description: Digitalization is becoming the foundational layer for next-generation Mining and Construction Equipment (MCE). GPS, sensors, and connectivity hardware are streaming data to fleet-management platforms, enabling real-time monitoring, remote diagnostics, and predictive maintenance. AI is being deployed for predictive quality control, downtime reduction, and generative AI for product customization. This shift transforms hardware into connected, intelligent systems, requiring OEMs to embed digital capabilities and develop interoperable platforms for mixed fleets.
forces.source_title: Pressing the Throttle: Unlocking India’s Mining and Construction Equipment Industry’s Potential

forces.title: Strong global demand for engineering goods drives exports
forces.description: Engineering goods remain India's largest export category, valued at US$ 122.52 billion in FY26 and projected to reach US$ 200 billion by 2030. This growth is driven by robust global demand for machinery, automobiles, auto components, and general industrial equipment. India's increasing credibility as an export base, especially in price-sensitive markets in Southeast Asia, Africa, the Gulf, and South America, provides significant opportunities for Capital Goods & Machinery manufacturers.
forces.source_title: Engineering And Capital Goods Industry In India

forces.title: Cybersecurity, cost, and talent scarcity hinder tech adoption in manufacturing
forces.description: Despite high ambition for technology adoption in industrial manufacturing, significant barriers exist. Cybersecurity, high costs, and scarcity of skilled resources and talent are major challenges. Insufficiently reliable data is also cited as a top AI risk. These factors necessitate substantial investment in data management, governance, and workforce upskilling to maximize return on technology investments and mitigate operational risks associated with advanced technology deployment.
forces.source_title: KPMG Global tech report 2026: Industrial Manufacturing

forces.title: Defence indigenisation boosts domestic manufacturing for military capital goods
forces.description: The Indian government's initiatives to strengthen indigenous defence manufacturing, including earmarking US$16.7 billion for domestic procurement and increasing R&D funding, significantly boost the order pipeline for local manufacturers. The 'Positive Indigenisation Lists' and schemes like ADITI, coupled with eased FDI norms (up to 74%), encourage domestic design, development, and production of military hardware, armored platforms, and specialized systems, directly benefiting defense-related capital goods manufacturers.

forces.title: Manufacturing PMI shows sustained expansion despite moderation
forces.description: India’s manufacturing Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) has consistently remained in the expansion zone (above 50) since March 2023, reaching 55.0 in May 2026. This indicates sustained expansion in manufacturing activity, driven by resilient demand, new orders, and output. While there has been a moderation in growth compared to previous years, the positive sentiment reflected by the PMI is a favorable cyclical trend supporting the Capital Goods & Machinery sector.

viewpoints.title: MCE sector crucial for India's growth, requires advanced equipment and collaboration
viewpoints.description: The Mining and Construction Equipment (MCE) sector holds a strategic position in India's growth agenda, with its performance influencing infrastructure creation and industrial expansion. Rising public and private investments, increasing project complexity, and higher productivity expectations are driving demand for more advanced equipment, greater efficiency, and stronger service capabilities. The next growth phase relies on deeper collaboration between industry, government, financial institutions, technology providers, academia, and end-users, alongside an enabling environment for investment, innovation, skill development, and ease of doing business.
viewpoints.source_title: Pressing the Throttle: Unlocking India’s Mining and Construction Equipment Industry’s Potential

viewpoints.title: India's MCE industry transformed from import-led to a global net exporter
viewpoints.description: India's Mining and Construction Equipment (MCE) industry has rapidly evolved from a small, import-dependent market to a genuine global growth platform. The country has emerged as a net exporter of MCE equipment, demonstrating the increasing prowess of its manufacturing sector. This shift highlights India's growing credibility as an export base and its potential to capture a larger share of the global market, moving beyond merely supporting domestic growth to actively shaping it.
viewpoints.source_title: Pressing the Throttle: Unlocking India’s Mining and Construction Equipment Industry’s Potential

viewpoints.title: MCE industry at inflection point, poised to lead through reinvention and technology
viewpoints.description: The Mining and Construction Equipment industry is at an inflection point, with India having the chance to lead global transformation rather than just catching up. This reinvention is driven by shifts to cleaner fuels, autonomous vehicles, and connected fleet ecosystems, where hardware evolves into intelligent systems. Indian players have a significant opportunity if they prioritize early investment in these technological changes, leveraging strong domestic demand and the chance to set the pace in a rapidly evolving global landscape.
viewpoints.source_title: Pressing the Throttle: Unlocking India’s Mining and Construction Equipment Industry’s Potential

viewpoints.title: Advanced technology and AI are driving competitive advantage and financial gains in industrial manufacturing
viewpoints.description: A significant majority (87%) of industrial manufacturing executives believe that advanced technology will be a key driver of future competitive advantage, with nearly half (49%) already reporting substantial financial gains from AI and intelligent technologies. This indicates a strong trend towards technology adoption and a clear understanding of its value proposition within the sector, pointing to continued investment and transformation across operations, quality control, and decision-making processes.
viewpoints.source_title: KPMG Global tech report 2026: Industrial Manufacturing

viewpoints.title: Government tax incentives to accelerate digital transformation in Indian industrial manufacturing
viewpoints.description: The Indian government's Budget 2026 announcement of long-term tax incentives for data center and digital infrastructure expenditure is expected to significantly accelerate digital transformation. This is particularly impactful for India's industrial manufacturing sector, where digital penetration currently lags behind some international players. The incentives are likely to attract foreign cloud service providers and multinational interest, fostering increased digitization momentum and enhancing the sector's overall competitiveness.
viewpoints.source_title: KPMG Global tech report 2026: Industrial Manufacturing

viewpoints.title: State capital outlay expected to rise, signaling continued investment focus
viewpoints.description: Aggregate state capital outlay is budgeted to increase by 15% in FY27, building on an already high growth of 25.2% estimated for FY26. This sustained focus on investment, along with stronger capital outlay growth compared to revenue expenditure, indicates a better quality of spending by states. This trend, supported by the Centre’s 50-year interest-free loans for capital investment, bodes well for the demand for capital goods and machinery.
